raw_response:
I am still going to lean on cotton this year. I have only 8 mu, and with people going out for work I cannot spread the family too thin, but I also do not want all the land in one crop. Cotton is what I know best and what I have managed for many years, so I will keep most of the land in cotton. I will leave a smaller piece for maize and a small piece for mungbean. Maize gives us grain and some steady output, and mungbean does not need as much fertilizer, so it helps me keep some cash in hand. I watch what the neighbors do. If spring stays dry, I will use the well once to get cotton up evenly, but I will not pour money into too many irrigations because pumping costs money. I usually do not chase the highest yield. I want the crop to come out safely and not leave me short of cash halfway through the season.

For cotton, I will plant on the better land and manage it a bit more carefully because that is where my cash income comes from. I will put base fertilizer down first, then add a second round when the plants are growing strong. For maize, I will keep it simple with one base application and one topdress, same as many people around here. Mungbean I will manage lightly. If I spend too much on that crop, it is hard to get the money back. With my age and family labor situation, I would rather keep the plan steady and manageable than make it too complicated.
